scripts.title: Ace Zaxy Super V3
scripts.features:
Script Description - AceZaxy Super V3

Here's the complete breakdown of what this script does:

What is it?

It's a Roblox script that creates a super cyberpunk loading screen + a full-featured interface (WindUI) with multiple features for manipulating parts, ESP, fly, and other functionalities.

Main Features:

🎨 Visual Interface (Loading Screen)

Ultra-stylized initial screen with cyberpunk theme (purple, cyan, neon)

Animated pulsing purple grid/grid animation

Floating neon particles

Retro CRT-style scanlines

Dark vignette on the edges

Progress bar with animation

Badge with random "fun facts"

🎮 Zaxy controller - Part Control

Controls up to 500 parts simultaneously

Different modes: Orbit, Knives, Cage, Float Wave, etc

Automatic Anti-Void (repositions parts that fall off the map)

Rainbow color pulsing system

👁️ ESP

Shows tracers (lines) of all players

Visualizes character skeletons

Shows names and distance

✈️ Fly/Movement

Flight system with smoothing

Smooth air control

Infinite SimulationRadius

🎵 Music System

Plays custom audio

Saves last track between sessions

Control via K button

💾 Auto-Save

Automatically saves settings to JSON

Restores settings on restart

🔐 Anti-Exploit

Locks stolen parts to the thief

⚙️ WindUI Interface

Main menu with multiple tabs (Ring, Wings, ESP, Fly, Settings, etc)

Customizable buttons with callbacks

Sliders for value adjustment

Toggle switches

comments.text: sir, your script is ai sir.
@WuzRERBorn Where did you see "ia" in the code?

@WuzRERBorn If you think it's a problem that I use AI to write the code, then simply don't use my script. *ody is forcing you to use it.

AI was just a tool. The entire idea behind the project, the game research, the features, the testing, the updates, and the detailed instructions given to the AI were all done by me. If it were as simple as saying "make me a script," any AI would generate generic code that would probably not even work properly.

It's funny to see people reduce months of work to "it's all AI" when they have no idea how projects like this are actually developed. Writing code is only one part of the process.

So before trying to discredit someone else's work, make sure you understand what you're talking about. And if you still think the script is bad simply because I used AI to write the code, the solution is very simple: don't use it. *ody spent their time developing this project to force you to click "execute."

@WuzRERBorn Calling it "an AI script" doesn't make it easily reproducible. If it were that simple, you would've recreated it already instead of complaining about it.

The AI didn't design the project. It didn't study the game, decide how the features should work, test them, or spend time improving them. I did. AI was only used to write the code from my specifications.

And yes, I obfuscate my code. It's my project, and I don't owe anyone the source code. Protecting my work isn't "dumb"—stealing or expecting developers to leave their code exposed is.

If you don't like it, don't use it. It's that simple.

scripts.title: God Mode
scripts.features:
god mode for natural disasters

Natural Disaster Survival god mode
scripts.script:
local players = game:GetService("Players")

local lp = players.LocalPlayer
local char = lp.Character or lp.CharacterAdded:Wait()
local hum = char:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
local rootpart = hum and hum.RootPart

if not rootpart then return end

local oldpos = rootpart.CFrame
hum:SetStateEnabled(Enum.HumanoidStateType.Dead, false)
rootpart.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.new(9e9, 9e9, 9e9)

task.wait(.5)

rootpart.AssemblyLinearVelocity = Vector3.zero
rootpart.AssemblyAngularVelocity = Vector3.zero

rootpart.CFrame = oldpos
